working_proof.proof: Use the ACTUAL proper strongly semistable formal model F of the given smooth projective curve X/C, with the finitely many actual C-rational marked points p reducing to DISTINCT smooth residual points q, constructed in working260 from whole BPR4.11 and puncture4.8. The complete immediate BPR statements/proofs were read in260; this is an ordinary source application, not an extra accepted grant or a claim that every recursively cited stable-reduction proof was reconstructed. This record addresses260.A3, leaving its other applications independently reviewable.

BPR Cor4.4 gives actual formal-etale standard-curve charts S(b)=Spf(R<x,y>/(xy-b)), b!=0, around EVERY point, with R=C-circle. The residue etale map preserves and reflects smoothness at the actual point, so the smooth residual q maps to the smooth part of the standard residual curve. At least one of x,y is consequently nonzero there; use x after exchanging them if necessary. On the corresponding formal open, x is a UNIT and y=b/x. Thus S(b) restricted there is the formal multiplicative coordinate chart Spf(R<t,u>/(tu-1)), with t=x. Its reductions modulo every a^j are Spec((R/a^j)[t,1/t]), etale over the polynomial affine line. The composition gives an actual formal-etale coordinate t on an affine formal neighborhood of q. This is a concrete application of the standard chart, not an inference that every topological open ball supplies such a coordinate.

For an actual affine formal chart U=Spf(A), BPR4.2(3) identifies A with the powerbounded ring of its actual affinoid generic domain. Each f in A therefore has |f(p)|<=1. The GIVEN point p defines a continuous R-algebra evaluation epsilon:A->R, restricting to the identity on R, and hence compatible evaluations modulo ALLa^j. Membership in U follows from red(p)=q in the residual open. Put c=t(p) in R and tau=t-c. The value c is a unit here, but only c in R is needed for the monic-polynomial argument. No completion of C(X) or model-algebraization assumption is needed.

The actual residual coordinate morphism is etale, so its fibre at c-tilde is zero dimensional reduced and finite on this affine chart, by Stacks29.37.7. Its points have finite separable residue extensions; C-tilde is algebraically closed since C is. For completeness, any monic polynomial over C-tilde lifts to R, splits over C, and all of its roots have norm<=1 by the dominant-monic-term argument; reduction of the factorization gives splitting over C-tilde. Choose a residual affine principal neighborhood D(f) containing q but excluding the other finitely many fibre points, using Chinese remainders on their distinct maximal ideals, and lift f to A. The actual p has |f(p)|=1, so it stays in the completed formal localization and all its coordinates remain bounded. Rename the resulting complete chart A. The residual zero fibre of tau is now exactly the ONE REDUCED rational point q.

The ideal(a) has finite ideal type and the actual formal chart morphism is adic. Whole FK1308.4734v5 I5.3.10/11 says formal-etale is equivalent to etaleness of every reduction modulo a^j; its immediate proof uses5.3.4/4.8.13. These exact units were ROOTread at LF17165-17316. Thus A_j=A/a^jA is etale over R_j[t], R_j=R/a^jR, for EVERYj>=1. Ordinary Stacks29.37.4/11/12 gives base change, finite presentation and flatness. In particular Q_j=A_j/(tau) is an affine etale R_j-algebra, and epsilon_j factors through Q_j as a retraction of R_j->Q_j.

Spec(R_j) has one point and its maximal ideal m/a^j is NIL, with no uniform exponent required. Its extension to Q_j is NIL too: any one element is a finite sum of terms with nil coefficients; those finitely many coefficients generate a nilpotent ideal. Hence Spec(Q_j) has the same underlying space as Spec(Q_j tensor_Rj C-tilde), which by A4 is the single point q. The retraction epsilon_j gives a SECTION of the unramified separated morphism Spec(Q_j)->Spec(R_j). Whole Stacks41.6.1, Tag024T, makes that section an OPEN immersion (and closed, since the morphism is affine). Its image contains q and therefore is ALLof Spec(Q_j); an open immersion with entire open image is an isomorphism. Consequently R_j->Q_j is an isomorphism with inverse epsilon_j. This does not presume that a mere one-point fibre identifies the residual field: the etale section and its open-immersion property prove the ring isomorphism. No finite-free-module theorem is needed for this alternative proof.

Multiplication by the MONIC polynomial t-c is injective on R_j[t] even though R_j has zero divisors: the highest nonzero coefficient of any nonzero polynomial remains its highest product coefficient. Flatness of the actual etale A_j over R_j[t] preserves this injection, so tau is a nonzerodivisor in every A_j. If tau*h=0 in A, then h is zero modulo all a^j; a-adic separation gives h=0. Thus tau is a genuine nonzerodivisor of the complete chart A, without requiring A to be an integral domain.

If h in A evaluates to0, A6 gives h modulo a^j= tau*q_j for EVERYj. The q_j are UNIQUE by A7. Reducing the equation for q_(j+1) modulo a^j and using uniqueness proves compatibility. A=lim_j A/a^jA gives q in A. Separation gives h=tau*q. Conversely every multiple of tau evaluates to0. Since constants map identically, epsilon is surjective and its EXACT kernel is(tau), giving A/(tau)=R with the ORIGINALevaluation. The ideal is closed as the kernel of a continuous map to separated R; its effectiveness and exact inverse limit are proved, rather than assumed for an unknown ideal. Inverting a gives the original C-rational generic zero p and no other zero.

On formal overlaps containing q, two such local equations define the same ORIGINALevaluation ideal and hence differ by a unit after restriction; the uniqueness/kernel proof is local and applies to the same bounded point. On the complement of q the equation is a formal unit. This also follows directly from the invertible reduction: for any finite coefficient error h in mA, choose a bound r<1 on its finitely many m-coefficients; then h^N belongs to a^jA for N large, so the geometric inverse converges in the complete chart. Thus the principal ideals glue with the unit ideal off q to an effective HORIZONTALformal Cartier divisor H_p whose generic zero is precisely p. The special quotient is the reduced rational point, so its degree contribution on the single component through q is exactly1; it has no contribution on other components because q is smooth and avoids nodes.

For the finitely many distinctly reducing marked points of the ORIGINALsection divisor div(S0)=sum n_p p of M=dL, the H_p are disjoint and H=sum n_p H_p is an actual formal Cartier divisor. Its generic bundle O_F(H)|X is EXACTLYM through S0. Its residual degrees are a_v=sum over p reducing to C_v n_p, all>=0 and sumdeg(M)=ddeg(L).
